frameworks.change: Preserve the existing framework reach and the Windows-only net472 condition. The front door and Workflows use the full framework set. net8.0 retirement belongs to a later release.

htmlDependency.today: ProjectReferences OfficeIMO.Word.Html and OfficeIMO.Markdown.Html, which bring OfficeIMO.Html and AngleSharp.

callSites.use: Raw HTML blocks and HTML comments in Markdown (BlockRenderer.cs:256, 262) are inserted through the Word HTML importer.
TryRenderHtmlFallbackViaMarkdownAst: HTML fragments are converted back to Markdown AST and rendered natively.

htmlDependency.otherUsings: MarkdownToWordConverter.cs, .Images.cs, .SharedRendering.cs, .Formatting.cs and .BlockRenderer.cs have "using OfficeIMO.Word.Html; using OfficeIMO.Markdown.Html;" but no other type use (verify at compile time).
removal: Add an internal raw-HTML hook to WordMarkdownImportOptions (for example Func<string, WordDocument, bool> or an IWordMarkdownHtmlRenderer interface) that defaults to a non-HTML fallback: emit the raw HTML as literal/code text and record an OfficeDiagnostic ("html-block-as-text").

OfficeIMO.Word.Html registers the real HTML renderer when present: either an opt-in extension (options.UseHtmlBlocks()) in OfficeIMO.Word.Html, or the OfficeIMO front door wires it so the default bundle keeps today's behavior.
Drop both ProjectReferences; OfficeIMO.Word.Markdown then references Core, Word and Markdown only.
Behavior change: users of OfficeIMO.Word.Markdown alone lose HTML-block fidelity unless they also install OfficeIMO.Word.Html (or OfficeIMO). Document in MIGRATION.md.
htmlDependency.readmeImpact: README mentions ToHtmlViaMarkdown/ToHtmlFragmentViaMarkdown/SaveAsHtmlViaMarkdown, which are not in the current public API (stale README to fix with M4).

openQuestions: Raw HTML blocks lose fidelity when only OfficeIMO.Word.Markdown is installed; acceptable default?

Static From{Source} on a type owned by another package (WordDocument.FromHtml in OfficeIMO.Word.Html, WordDocument.FromMarkdown, MarkdownDocument.FromHtml, WordDocument.FromPdf) is only possible with C# 14 static extension members. The SDK supports them for netstandard2.0 targets, but callers on older language versions (.NET Framework projects default to C# 7.3, Windows PowerShell) must call the containing static class directly. Alternative: keep instance forms on the source (pdf.ToWord(), html.ToWordDocument()) as the only adapter shape.

designResolutions.formatEnum: OfficeDocumentFormat; no OfficeFormat enum is introduced.
designResolutions.conversionDirection: Instance extensions on the source document; no static From factories.
designResolutions.asyncReports: OfficeConversionResult<T> carries the converted value and OfficeConversionReport.
designResolutions.frontDoorTarget: OfficeIMO, its batch engine, OfficeIMO.Workflows and OfficeIMO.Workflows.IWork target netstandard2.0, net8.0 and net10.0, plus net472 through the existing Windows-only project condition (approved c526a10ad2). Modern-only route engines are conditionally referenced and registered.
designResolutions.frameworks: Superseded by the approved c526a10ad2 design: retain netstandard2.0, net8.0, net10.0 and the original Windows-only net472 declaration; modern-only packages retain their original targets. Front door and Workflows gain the full set, with explicitly conditional modern engines.
designResolutions.modernAnalysis: Directory.Build.targets enables IsAotCompatible, EnableTrimAnalyzer and EnableAotAnalyzer for packable production library builds targeting net8.0/net10.0. Qualification remains in progress; older targets do not enable those analyzers.

phaseA.scope: Package boundaries, target frameworks, lifecycle, options, conversions and names.

additionalChanges.old: Raw HTML fragment processing imports Word.Html and Markdown.Html.
additionalChanges.new: Internal raw-HTML rendering and parsing callbacks plus html-block-as-text diagnostics.
additionalChanges.reason: The adapter retains only the Word and Markdown engines; the front door can supply HTML processing.

extraChanges.subject: Direct raw HTML fidelity boundary
extraChanges.note: The direct adapter does not load a third format engine. Internal raw-HTML renderer/parser hooks allow the front door to supply richer HTML conversion; literal fallback emits html-block-as-text.

extraChanges.subject: Caller-owned template import
extraChanges.note: WordMarkdownImportOptions.Template and placeholder properties absorb the separate template bag; caller-owned templates are never disposed on a loss rejection.

extraChanges.subject: Raw HTML hook diagnostics
extraChanges.note: Internal renderer/parser hooks receive the active per-operation diagnostic sink after option cloning. The front door can preserve HTML stage severity, location, component and loss without an HTML dependency in the direct adapter.

Async conversion entry points capture options before deferred work or resource awaits. The same snapshot supplies resource/size limits and final FailOnLoss acceptance; caller-owned template documents and callbacks retain their ownership.

The consolidated import options preserve the former template defaults: front matter is hidden when Template is set unless RenderFrontMatter is explicitly chosen. Standalone imports still render front matter by default; options capture preserves the explicit/unset distinction.

Synchronous file and stream saves retain cancellation through publication using OfficeFileCommit and OfficeStreamWriter.CopyBytes. Empty lifetime try/finally blocks were removed; template documents retain caller ownership.

Omitted running content, explicit page breaks and unsupported content emit typed omission diagnostics. Image and SVG sidecars are staged until loss acceptance, preventing analysis or rejected saves from changing destination assets.
The merged transcript factory replaces its raw visualMaxWidthPx argument with OfficeLength? visualMaxWidth. Maintained README and transcript/cross-pipeline consumers use the options factory directly.
Markdown import and retained tests use attached field, link and equation models, selecting Paragraph where paragraph formatting is required.

applicationStatus: Phase A applied and validated on the supported macOS targets. Phase B and Tier 2 entries retain their status; Windows .NET Framework validation remains pending.
authority: Docs/officeimo.api-design.md, including the c526a10ad2 framework decision; the approved design overrides M0 open questions.

questionResolutions.conversionForms: Source.ToTarget, source.SaveAsTarget and OfficeConversionReport; async ToTarget returns OfficeConversionResult<T>. ToHtml returns string. No static From factories.
questionResolutions.frameworks: No framework is dropped in 3.6. Original library TFMs and Windows net472 conditions remain; the front door and both Workflows projects support the full set. Modern-only engines stay conditional.
questionResolutions.packageDirection: Word.Pdf and PowerPoint.Pdf export native documents. Reverse reconstruction is Pdf.Word and Pdf.PowerPoint; Excel reconstruction is Pdf.Excel. Word page images live in Word.Pdf.
questionResolutions.surface: Markdown syntax nodes are exempt from the format prefix. OfficeColor/OfficeColorRole use the root OfficeIMO namespace. Authoring, units, image-builder consolidation, visibility baselines and AOT smoke acceptance are Phase B.
